title: Commercial proposal & pricing playbook for SaaS platform customers
author: Priya Patel
content:
Executive summary:

This document is a field-ready commercial proposal template and pricing playbook aimed at SaaS platform and mid-market accounts evaluating embedded LLM features (chat, generation, embeddings, and reranking). It pairs a concise positioning brief, competitor differentiators, a negotiated pricing framework, and a short security FAQ that reps can drop into RFPs and sales decks. Use this to accelerate deal cycles while preserving margin and minimizing enterprise risk.

Who this is for:
- Account executives and solutions engineers working with platform/product leaders at SaaS businesses (ARR $5M–$150M).
- Pre-sales and commercial leaders designing subscription and usage proposals.

Key selling themes (1-sentence hooks):
- Deliver consistent, production-grade LLM inference that reduces per-request cost while guaranteeing predictable latency and availability.
- Move from experimentation to productization with a single runtime across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes — one integration, consistent observability.
- Optimize cost with batching, KV caching, quantization, and routing controls that preserve output quality.

Value props mapped to buyer personas:
- Platform/CTO: Unified runtime across cloud and private deployments; predictable performance SLOs and reserved capacity options for critical flows.
- Product lead: Out-of-the-box observability (token cost, per-route latency) and rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallbacks) reduce feature risk.
- Finance/Platform Ops: Cost levers (quant profiles, batching) and clear unit economics to forecast OPEX.

Competitive brief (concise analysis):
- Major competitors: Managed LLM endpoints from hyperscalers, API-first providers, and self-hosted inference runtimes.
- Redwood differentiators:
  - Production-first SLAs and deterministic latency tuning (policy-based routing + fallback variants).
  - Unified interface across Hosted/Dedicated/Private reduces integration and audit surface.
  - Cost tooling (Optimize) that recommends quantization and batching for workload patterns — measurable savings during PoC.
- Typical competitor objections and rebuttals:
  - "Hyperscalers are cheaper for GPUs": Hyperscaler unit costs can be lower at scale but lack Redwood’s inference-level batching, KV caching, and automatic routing by cost/latency — often leading to higher consumed token cost for the same latency envelope.
  - "We already have an internal runtime": Internal runtimes can be brittle; Redwood reduces operational burden with managed observability, rollout controls, and MTTI/MTTR guarantees for inference incidents.

Pricing guidance — principles and anchor examples:
Principles:
1. Separate access (subscription / reserved capacity) from consumption (hosted tokens, embeddings).
2. Preserve list price as anchor; offer SKU-level short-term concessions tied to usage ramps and multi-year commitments.
3. Protect margin by tying deepest discounts to reserved capacity or multi-year minimums, not pure token discounts.

Anchor pricing (examples — use as starting points; tailor by region and customer size):
- Hosted API (self-serve / small accounts):
  - Generation: $0.0025 per 1k prompt tokens + $0.015 per 1k generated tokens (example small LLM); adjust by model class.
  - Embeddings: $0.0005 per embedding (128-d baseline) with volume tiers at 250k, 1M embeddings.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity):
  - Entry reserved pool (4x T4-equivalent GPUs): $30k/month committed — includes baseline throughput SLA and 99.9% control-plane uptime SLA.
  - Medium pool (8+ A100-style capacity): $110k/month committed — includes priority scaling, 24x7 support, and monthly account review.
- Private / On-prem: license + platform fee model (example): $200k initial deployment + $25k/month support/updates for mid-market on-prem packages.

Negotiation levers (what to offer, when, and what to require in return):
- Trial credits: Offer $15k–$50k credits to validate performance and unit economics for 30–90 days. Require a technical onboarding and joint test plan.
- Ramp discounts: 10–25% on token rates for 6–12 months tied to usage milestones (e.g., hitting 20M tokens/month).
- Reserved capacity credits: Apply onboarding credit or first-month discount for multi-month reserved purchases.
- Professional services: Charge for integration and eval harness unless strategic. Offer a one-time deployment credit for multi-year commitments.
- Price protection: Offer a 6–12 month price lock when customers sign an annual committed contract.

Pricing redlines to avoid:
- Deep per-token discounts without committed minimums.
- Open-ended SLAs without caps or runbook/observability obligations.
- Commitments to bespoke model changes or custom kernels outside standard onboarding work.

Sample commercial proposal template (sales can copy/paste and edit):

--- Proposal: Redwood Inference — Embedded AI Platform for {CustomerName} ---
Proposal owner: {AE name} | SE: {SE name} | Date: {YYYY-MM-DD}
Summary of need:
- {CustomerName} requires low-latency, cost-predictable LLM inference for product features: search relevance, chat assistant, and embeddings for personalization.
Scope & deliverables:
- Hosted API access for development and initial production: up to 30M tokens/month + 1M embeddings included for first 90 days.
- Optional Dedicated pool (8 GPU-equivalent) for peak throughput with SLA commitments during production cutover.
Pricing (initial 12 months):
- Hosted usage: generation tokens at $0.0020 / 1k prompt tokens + $0.012 / 1k generated tokens with ramp discounts at 20M tokens/month.
- Dedicated: $95,000 / month committed pool (8-GPU equiv) with 30% ramp credit on month 1.
- Onboarding & integration: $25,000 (one-time) includes eval harness and three integration workshops.
Commercial terms & milestones:
1) PO or MSA signed (T+0) — receive onboarding credit and access to sandbox environment.
2) Production rollout (T+45) — Dedicated pool live or Hosted scaled to production.
3) Review & optimize (T+90) — Redwood Optimize recommendations report and cost-savings forecast.
Security and compliance summary (short):
- Data handling: Can operate in Hosted, Dedicated, or Private / VPC modes. For sensitive data we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS.
- Certifications: SOC 2 Type II (attestation available on request).
- Auditability: Token-level logging (obfuscated PII by default), configurable audit retention.
- Encryption: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest; KMS/HSM integration available for Private deployments.
Acceptance & next steps:
- Customer signs SOW / MSA for initial committed term.
- Redwood SE schedules onboarding call and joint test plan within 3 business days.

Security FAQ for prospect RFPs (insertable snippets):
Q: Where does customer data reside when using Hosted API?
A: Customer data can be routed to region-specific Redwood-hosted clusters. For regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments; we also support data residency controls and encryption keys managed by the customer (KMS).

Q: Do you support Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) or HSM?
A: Yes. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. For Dedicated we offer optional KMS integration on request.

Q: What logs are available for audits?
A: We provide request/response metadata at token granularity (raw outputs are optionally logged, default is obfuscated) along with system-level metrics, access logs, and change history for model rollouts. Retention windows can be customized under enterprise contracts.

Q: Do you support HIPAA / PCI use-cases?
A: Redwood supports customers with regulated workloads via Private deployments and contractual controls (BAA for HIPAA workloads where Private deployment is used). For PCI, we provide guidance for segmentation and can scope an on-prem packaging that meets cardholder data environment requirements.

Negotiation checklist (pre-sign):
- Confirm deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and region(s).
- Define clear SLA targets (latency SLOs, uptime, support response times). Example SLA anchors: 99.5% uptime for Hosted API control plane; Dedicated customers: 99.9% compute availability with seasonal scaling windows.
- Agree on audit logging scope and retention.
- Define rollback/fallback policies (which model variants to auto-fallback to) and test plan for failover.

Rapid rebuttal card (for AE/SE practice):
- "We’re concerned about cost": We’ll run a 30–60 day controlled PoC, provide Optimize recommendations, and quantify per-feature unit economics.
- "We need strict residency": Private deployments with BYOK and air-gapped options are available with defined lead time.
- "We need model control": Model pinning, rollout controls, and automatic fallback reduce risk — included in Dedicated and Private packages.

Case study snapshot — AcmeAnalytics (fictionalized template for field use):
Challenge: AcmeAnalytics needed sub-200ms median inference latency for interactive recommendations while controlling per-query cost across global customers.
Solution: Deployed a hybrid approach: Hosted for low-volume regional flows + Dedicated pool for peak east-coast traffic; applied Redwood Optimize suggestions (KV prefix caching + 4-bit quantization variant for tail requests).
Outcome: 35% reduction in median latency, 42% reduction in per-query inference cost in first 90 days, accelerated rollout from PoC to 80% of paid traffic in 60 days.

Operational handoffs (owner assignments — copy into deal docs):
- AE: commercial negotiation and contract sign-off.
- SE: performance validation, eval harness, and production cutover checklist.
- CS/Customer Success: first 90-day optimization plan and QBR schedule.
- Support/Engineering on-call: defined escalation path for inference incidents (link to runbook).

Appendix B — Suggested slide outline for customer pitch deck:
1) Problem / Context (customer-specific)
2) Redwood value props & product fit
3) Arch options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with performance & cost tradeoffs
4) Commercial proposal summary and timeline
5) Security, compliance & audit commitments
6) Case study & references
7) Next steps / decision calendar

How to use this doc:
- Copy the proposal template into an editable Google Doc, replace anchors ({}), and attach the suggested SOW appendix for legal.
- Attach the short security FAQ to any RFP response.
- Run the Optimize PoC checklist after signing a trial credit MOU.

Owners and maintenance cadence:
- Playbook owner: go-to-market enablement (Priya Patel).
- Technical reviewer cadence: quarterly or when pricing tiers change.
- Legal and security sign-off required for any changes to the Security FAQ or SLA anchors.
